source_gaps.missing_claim: V4 is installed and has completed account-authenticated generation, review, verification, publication, and exact-head merge probes on the live host.
source_gaps.why_missing: Implementation and deterministic verification precede attended host activation. The account-authenticated live probes require explicit owner risk acceptance and must not run as part of ordinary repository tests.

blocks.title: Explicit unsupported-use exception
blocks.text: CloudX V4 uses a locally logged-in Codex account because the owner explicitly rejected API-key authentication. OpenAI's account-auth automation guide says not to use this workflow for public or open-source repositories. V4 therefore fails closed unless the operator records the explicit risk acceptance. The controls below reduce repository and host exposure; they do not make this use officially supported.

Privileged AI execution moves out of GitHub Actions. Public CloudX keeps GitHub-hosted CI, classification, and free public-repository rulesets. A private source repository supplies reviewed controller code, but the host's root-owned exact SHA and source digest are the runtime trust anchor.

claims.text: OpenAI does not support persistent ChatGPT account authentication for automation against a public or open-source repository, so V4 records an explicit exception and fails closed without it.

evidence.locator: Maintain Codex account auth in CI/CD, guidance and when-to-use sections
evidence.excerpt: The guide identifies API keys as the normal automation choice, limits account auth to trusted private automation, and says not to use it for public or open-source repositories.
Activation fails closed unless the owner records the explicit unsupported-public-repository risk acceptance requested in this task.

claims.text: V4 replaces private GitHub Actions dispatch with a locally pinned durable controller and separated execution services.

evidence.excerpt: The reviewed plan removes privileged workflows, the Actions runner, private environments, and the Controller Dispatcher App.
GitHub warns that untrusted workflow code can persistently compromise a self-hosted runner and says such runners should almost never be used for public repositories.

claims.text: CloudX public branch policy remains in public-repository rulesets available on GitHub Free.

evidence.excerpt: GitHub documents rulesets as available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations.
The public policy retains the two CloudX main-branch rulesets and removes private controller protection assumptions.

visuals.purpose: Show that public GitHub, durable state, model auth, publication, and merge authority are separate.
visuals.alt_text: CloudX public repository sends signed events to an intake manager, which owns durable executions. A credential-free executor talks separately to a logged-in Codex worker, verifier, Publisher actuator, and Merge actuator.
visuals.caption: V4 separates durable state, account authentication, candidate verification, publication, and merge credentials.

blocks.text: The model sees a controller-generated bounded context through standard input. Repository instructions, hooks, plugins, MCP configuration, credential files, links, special files, binary content, and oversized content cannot become model authority. Codex runs in one serialized stream with an ephemeral read-only sandbox, ignored user and repository rules, no shell tool, a fixed model configuration, an output schema, and bounded process supervision.

claims.text: Intake, execution, Codex authentication, verification, publication, and merge have distinct credentials and service identities.

evidence.locator: systemd units, sockets, Compose secrets, and setup role manifests
evidence.excerpt: Service users, credential files, and socket modes separate the Target, Codex, Publisher, and Merge authorities.
Finite plans route through typed one-time actuator requests without command or environment fields.

claims.text: Codex receives only bounded controller material and runs without repository instruction authority, shell access, GitHub credentials, or concurrent access to auth.json.

evidence.excerpt: The executor canonicalizes text context, rejects authority-bearing paths, scrubs the environment, builds one exact read-only shell-free Codex command, bounds the process group, and serializes jobs.
OpenAI documents codex exec for pipelines with explicit sandbox settings, ephemeral mode, JSONL events, and output schemas.

tables.caption: Each authority receives only the credential required for its fixed operation.
rows: Signed webhook intake, exact subject reads, durable execution state
Fixed plans, workspace lifecycle, cancellation, typed routing
Exact patch, subject, base, path, and model-review validation before publication
Candidate branch, pull request, labels, and checks
One exact-head managed merge after live authorization

items: The manager creates one deduplicated execution bound to the target identity, controller commit, controller source digest, and bounded payload.
One executor claims the execution once, heartbeats its lease, and moves it through fixed controller-owned stages.
An expired claimed or running lease becomes uncertain and requires explicit operator recovery; it is never automatically retried.
Managed publication is bound to a canonical post-verification artifact; candidate code executes only later in public GitHub-hosted CI.
Publisher and Merge actuators independently validate typed one-time requests and re-fetch the current subject before acting.

blocks.text: A current writer authorizes the exact issue revision or pull request head before any account-authenticated model work is queued.
V4 enables managed generated-change automerge. Actorless ordinary and protected-manual merge requests are rejected until manager admission durably binds the authorizing human identity.

claims.text: V4 executions have manager-owned identity, deduplication, one-attempt leases, heartbeats, append-only transitions, bounded terminal evidence, and explicit uncertain recovery.

evidence.locator: migration 013 and local execution domain, service, and repository
evidence.excerpt: The V4 state resource records exact controller and target identity, pending through terminal states, one attempt, lease capability hashes, events, result digests, and sanitized failures.

claims.text: Public input cannot trigger account-authenticated work until a current writer authorizes the exact subject.

evidence.excerpt: The policy names separate issue approval and exact pull request model-request labels.
The manager verifies the current label, actor permission, and exact head before enqueue.

blocks.text: Setup accepts one explicit reviewed 40-character controller commit and canonical source digest. It installs a root-owned release, records an append-only local ledger, and starts hardened service users and sockets. It configures the three public-target Apps and CloudX public rulesets. It also verifies that the private repository has no Actions runner, workflow, secret, variable, or environment authority. A private tag is informational, not a trust root.

The V4 migration refuses to switch while any V3 workflow execution or registration state is active or ambiguous. Operators resolve those records first. Terminal V3 audit history remains read-only; V4 does not add a compatibility execution path.

claims.text: The runtime trust anchor is an attended root-owned exact release, not mutable private GitHub protection.

evidence.excerpt: Setup validates the exact commit and tracked-source digest, installs read-only release content, switches one local current pointer, and appends a root-owned ledger record.

claims.text: Private GitHub Actions, environments, secrets, variables, runner registration, and the Controller Dispatcher authority are retired rather than protected by a paid plan.

evidence.locator: RetiredGitHubActions.mjs and three-role App manifest setup
evidence.excerpt: Setup removes and verifies absence of the retired Actions resources and provisions only Target, Publisher, and Merge roles.

claims.text: V4 is an intentional breaking authority migration that blocks on active or ambiguous V3 execution state.

evidence.excerpt: The migration raises an error instead of translating an active or ambiguous workflow execution into local authority.
Operators resolve nonterminal V3 state before migration; terminal audit data remains read-only.

blocks.title: Code complete is not host activated
blocks.text: Repository tests, migration integration, static systemd verification, Compose checks, coverage, security review, and exact pushed commits are required before release. Account-authenticated live probes are a separate attended gate after explicit risk acceptance. Until those probes pass, V4 is implemented but not activated.

claims.text: Live host activation remains a separate evidence gap after repository implementation and deterministic verification.

evidence.locator: required proof and live activation verification
evidence.excerpt: The reviewed plan separates deterministic repository verification from installed-service and account-authenticated live activation probes.
